title: Scared of the Air Puff

patient.name: Mdm Chong Mei Ling
patient.presenting_complaint: At a screening station; very anxious about the air-puff tonometer and keeps flinching, giving inconsistent readings

history.hpc: Mdm Chong is at the NCT screening station but is very nervous. She says: 'The air puff make me scared, I keep blinking and pull back.' The first few NCT attempts give widely inconsistent readings. The OT must settle the patient, improve technique, obtain reliable readings, and decide when to escalate to Goldmann tonometry.
history.social_hx: Works at a hawker stall. Non-smoker. Generally anxious in clinical settings.

investigations.nct_screening: Initial NCT readings inconsistent due to blinking/flinching. The OT reassured the patient, demonstrated the puff on her hand, asked her to keep both eyes open and look at the target, and re-attempted. Consistent readings were then obtained (RE 16, LE 15 mmHg). Two common causes of unreliable NCT are blinking/poor cooperation and poor positioning/alignment.

diagnosis: Initially unreliable NCT due to patient anxiety and blinking, resolved with reassurance and better technique to give consistent normal readings. The OT competency is recognising unreliable readings, correcting technique, and knowing that persistently unreliable NCT should be referred for Goldmann tonometry.

immediate: Recognise the widely inconsistent readings as unreliable, not true IOP values
Reassure the patient and explain/demonstrate the air puff (e.g., on the back of her hand) to reduce fear
Optimise technique: correct positioning and alignment, ask her to keep both eyes open and fixate the target
Re-attempt and confirm the readings are now consistent before recording
Document the technique used and the final consistent readings
If readings remain unreliable despite this, refer for Goldmann applanation tonometry
follow_up: If unable to obtain reliable NCT, arrange Goldmann tonometry
Record the screening outcome and any difficulty for future reference
Advise routine follow-up as per screening protocol
patient_education: Reassure her the puff is harmless and quick, and demonstrate it to ease anxiety
Coach her to keep both eyes open and look straight at the light
Explain why a steady, unflinching moment is needed for an accurate reading
Praise her cooperation once reliable readings are obtained

key_points: Identifies the patient's anxiety and blinking as the source of difficulty
Confirms the screening context and relevant history
Confirms glasses/lenses removed and no contraindication
Explains and demonstrates the procedure to reduce fear
Recognises the inconsistent readings as unreliable rather than true IOP
Optimises positioning, alignment, and patient cooperation before repeating
Identifies common causes of unreliable NCT (blinking, poor alignment)
Understands when NCT readings are unreliable
Knows persistently unreliable NCT should be referred for Goldmann tonometry
Interprets the final consistent readings as normal
Does not record an artefactual reading as the result
Reassures and coaches the patient to obtain reliable readings
Documents technique and the final consistent readings
Escalates to Goldmann tonometry if NCT stays unreliable
